Subject: Urgent: Increasing 429s and timeouts impacting inference P99

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 429s and P99 timeouts on hosted API this morning around 10:30am PT. Our service layer is getting a stream of 429 responses, then immediately retrying (we observed a lot of tight retries from our side — we have since added jitter). The net effect is long tail latency spikes and ~2% of requests outright timing out after 30s. This is affecting our user-facing search-as-you-type product.

Attached is a short log extract with request IDs and timestamps plus a sample of rate-limit headers from two requests. High-level numbers: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms (normal for us), p99 spiking to 6-8s with a handful of timeouts. The 429 volume correlates with the P99 windows.

We need immediate mitigation and a timeline for a fix. Can you confirm:
- Is this a platform-wide degradation or isolated to our tenant?
- Will you consider temporarily lifting the strict 429 enforcement for our workload while the root cause is investigated?

We are copying ops@ and procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform
Citrine Labs

Alex/Vanessa — I'm leading SRE on this. Initial read: we've observed correlated 429 bursts across several tenants in the us-west-2 POP starting ~10:25am PT. We're looking at autoscaling signals plus ingress rate-limit enforcement.

Preliminary observations:
- The platform emitted a spike of 429s when a subset of tenant traffic hit a shared ingress throttling gate while downstream GPU queues were near 85% utilization.
- Some client SDKs (not necessarily Citrine's) are retrying aggressively without randomized jitter; that appears to amplify the tail.
- Our rate-limit policy currently returns 429 with X-RateLimit-ReleasedAfter in some cases, but not always a Retry-After header — we saw inconsistent headers in the attached snapshot. We're patching header consistency now.

Immediate mitigations (working now):
1) Temporarily increase per-tenant burst window for Citrine by 2x (will take effect within 5 minutes) — done for test bucket, rolling to production if metrics look good.
2) Enable a short-lived global backoff gate that introduces server-side 50–200ms randomized delay for clients exceeding soft thresholds to avoid synchronized retries (will deploy in 15–30 minutes).
3) Patch to always return Retry-After when 429 is due to server-side throttling (hotfix rolling).

We need Citrine to confirm any client-side retry loops and reduce retry aggressiveness while we stabilize.

I'll share request-ids and a more detailed timeline in the next update.

– Diego
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — we confirmed on our side that a new client release removed jitter in an attempt to reduce overall latency. We reverted that change and re-enabled exponential backoff with jitter; we also reduced max retries from 5 to 2.

Metrics already look better for the next minute, but we are still seeing occasional high p99s. We appreciate the quick bump. Two asks:
1) Please confirm the temporary per-tenant burst bump and any telemetry you can surface (which metrics will you monitor so we can correlate?).
2) If this recurs during peak, we will need a durable plan — e.g., routing critical traffic to a dedicated pool or capacity reservation. What is the path and rough timeline for that?

Alex
